ECON 500: Mathematical Economics: Applications of Mathematical Techniques to Economics.
ECON 501: Econometrics: Applications of Statistical Techniques to Economics
ECON 502: Economic behavior under pure and imperfect competition; price and output determination in product markets; prices and employment in factor markets.
ECON 503: National income accounts; determination of income, employment, interest rates, and the price level; stabilization policy.
ECON 507: Theory of international trade and investment; effect of commercial policy on trade and income distribution; multinational corporations and international trade.
ECON 510: General linear model, multicolinearity, specification error, autocorrelation, heteroskedasticity, restricted least squares, functional form, dummy variables, limited dependent variables.
ECON 512A: The course will provide a foundation for students in the computational methods used to numerically solve and simulate economic models and program econometric estimators.
ECON 512B: The course will provide continued exposure to the computational methods used to numerically solve and simulate economic models and program econometric estimators.
ECON 517: The balance of payments, portfolio allocation, monetary and fiscal policy in an open economy, exchange rate regimes, selected policy issues.
ECON 521: Theory of consumer behavior; theory of the firm; price determination in product and factor markets; introduction to welfare economics.
ECON 522: Measurement of income; theories of consumption, investment, and money holdings; static determination of income and employment; introduction to dynamic analysis.
ECON 530: This course is a workshop designed to guide students through the process of conducting independent research towards successful completion of the M.A. Scholar Essay project.
ECON 531: This course is a workshop designed to guide students through the process of conducting independent research towards successful completion of the Master's Scholarly Essay.
ECON 533: This course combines the use of econometric software and real economic data sets to study actual empirical questions in economics.
ECON 534: Foundations of current research in game theory.
ECON 543: The structure of American industry; performance and behavior; public policies toward business.
ECON 558: Classical and neoclassical quantity theories of money and contemporary criticism; Keynesian monetary theory and its critics.
ECON 559: Post-Keynesian reformulation of quantity and Keynesian theories of money; liquidity and general equilibrium approaches; current issues in theory and policy.
ECON 570: Resources and institutions; quantitative measures; theories of economic growth in developing areas; developmental policies.
ECON 589: Theories and methods relevant to the application of statistical methods to economics.
ECON 596: Creative projects, including nonthesis research, which are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
ECON 597: Formal courses given on a topical or special interest subject which may be offered infrequently; several different topics may be taught in one year or term.
